topic: What operational constraints limit optimal beam-to-beam channel allocation in mesh-type communication when using digital channelizers?
consensus_response: The primary operational constraint limiting optimal beam-to-beam channel allocation in mesh-type communication using digital channelizers is the limited processing frequency bandwidth (BW) of digital channelizers, which restricts simultaneous beam processing. This limitation is exacerbated by the fixed frequency bandwidth allocated to each destination beam, making it impossible to accommodate large traffic demands. As a result, the system's ability to adapt to changing traffic demands is reduced, leading to decreased average used bandwidth (AUB), increased average unused offered capacity (AUOC), and reduced average satisfaction index (ASI).
